newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia sees steady 1997 inflation, faster growth.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia sees steady 1997 inflation, faster growth.

text.p: Slovenia's government-sponsored Institute of Macroeconomic Analysis and Development on Wednesday forecast steady inflation next year and a pick-up in economic growth.

The insititute said it expected inflation to remain around nine percent, compared with 8.6-9.0 percent in 1996, while economic growth should accelerate to four percent from a projected 3.5 percent this year.
"Inflation is not likely to decrease significantly next year because of likely increases in the price of petrol and some other goods," institute head Janez Potocnik told a news conference.
The government has said it is considering a significant increase in petrol prices at the start of 1997. Slovenian petrol prices are currently among the lowest in Europe.
The institute said the economy should receive a boost next year as growth accelerated in Slovenia's main trading partner the European Union. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
